chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, saying: He (Al-Himyari) narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Jama'ah as-Sa'igh, who said: I heard al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar asking Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Does Allah impose obedience upon a servant and then conceal the news of the heavens from him?' He (Abu Abdullah) said to him: 'Allah is more exalted, more generous, more compassionate to His servants, and more merciful than to impose obedience upon a servant and then conceal the news of the heavens from him morning and evening.' (He said): Then Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) appeared. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Does it please you to look at the keeper of the book of Ali?' Al-Mufadhdhal said to him: 'And what else would please me more than that?' He said: 'This is the keeper of the book of Ali; the hidden book about which Allah said, "None shall touch it save the purified ones."'

key_terms.خَبَرَ السَّمَاءِ: News of the heavens (divine revelation or heavenly knowledge)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: The keeper/custodian of the book of Ali
key_terms.لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ: None shall touch it save the purified ones (Quranic verse)

ai.seo_question: Who is the keeper of Imam Ali's hidden book according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq uses this dialogue to affirm the principle of divine justice (Adl), arguing that God’s mercy precludes commanding obedience while withholding the necessary means of verification, thereby validating the necessity of clear, accessible revelation. The narration culminates in identifying Musa ibn Ja'far (al-Kazim) as the 'Sahib al-Kitab' (Keeper of the Book), linking him to the Quranic description of 'al-Mutahharun' (the Purified Ones) to underscore his unique spiritual status and authority. This connection reinforces the Shia belief in the infallible Imams as the living custodians of divine knowledge and the 'hidden book' of Ali.
